open-market-competition-imports.text: The research found no party position since 2021 on opening the market to more competition and imports, and the party has published no cost-of-living plan since 2021. Its tentative indication points to direct help for households, based on Gantz's 2024-2026 votes for benefits aimed at specific groups, mainly reservists.

cut-taxes-and-government-spending.text: The research found no documented party position on cutting taxes and government spending, and the party has published no cost-of-living plan since 2021. Its tentative indication points to direct help for households, based on Gantz's 2024-2026 votes for benefits aimed at specific groups, mainly reservists.

active-state-regulation.text: The research found no documented party position on stronger state supervision of prices, and the party has published no cost-of-living plan since 2021. Its tentative indication points to direct help for households, based on Gantz's 2024-2026 votes for benefits aimed at specific groups, mainly reservists.

direct-support-for-households.text: The research places the party closest to your answer, but only tentatively: it rests on Gantz's votes for benefits aimed at specific groups, mainly reservists, such as state funding of daycare fees for reservists' children (March and December 2025). No party cost-of-living plan since 2021 was found.

emergency-powers-shin-bet.text: Gantz voted against a bill on 10 December 2025 that would let a crime organization be declared a terror organization on a request from the head of the Shin Bet, and against a bill on holding people without trial for terror-organization membership on 3 July 2024. The party's documented approach is tougher weapons enforcement under ordinary law.

more-police-resources-normal-law.text: This is the closest match to the party's record, though no detailed party plan was found: Gantz voted for private bills raising penalties for holding illegal weapons (5 February 2025) and fining people who hold them (29 October 2025). He also voted for a 15 July 2024 no-confidence motion over rising crime.

invest-in-arab-communities-first.text: The party's documented approach is different: Gantz voted for tougher weapons-enforcement bills in February and October 2025 and for a July 2024 no-confidence motion over rising crime. The research found no documented party position on investing in Arab local councils.

resume-fighting-full-control.text: The party shares one element of your answer: on 5 February 2025 Gantz called creating safe areas outside Gaza for residents who choose to leave "admirable", and in an August 2026 interview he said Palestinians who wish to leave voluntarily may do so. In the same interview he said there should be no Israeli settlement in Gaza, which your answer would allow.

hold-positions-disarmament-first.text: This is a secondary element of the party's position: on 2 August 2026 Gantz wrote that Israel cannot compromise on Hamas's full disarmament before retreating from further territory. The party's main position is to defeat Hamas and then keep Israeli security control.

advance-international-arrangement.text: This is a secondary element of the party's position: in May 2024, as a war cabinet minister, Gantz called for an international civilian governance mechanism for Gaza with American, European, Arab and Palestinian elements. His main position is to defeat Hamas and keep Israeli security control, and in August 2026 he said Israel keeps full security superiority.

end-war-full-withdrawal.text: The party's documented position is to defeat Hamas and keep Israeli security control. On 2 August 2026 Gantz wrote that Israel cannot compromise on Hamas's full disarmament before retreating from further territory, and in an August 2026 interview he said Israel keeps full security superiority.

defeat-hamas-then-security-control.text: That is the party's main recorded position: in May 2024 Gantz set goals including toppling Hamas rule, demilitarizing Gaza and gaining Israeli security control. In an August 2026 interview he said there should be no Israeli settlement in Gaza and that Israel keeps full security superiority.

anchor-torah-study-exemption.text: Gantz voted against the final reading of the government's Security Service Law on 14 July 2026, which froze enforcement against yeshiva students who study at least 45 hours a week. On 3 September 2026 he said that everyone at 18 must serve.

gradual-targets-by-agreement.text: The party shares the aim of bringing Haredim into service, with state money tied to serving, but no longer backs the gradual route. As Defense Minister, Gantz voted for the 2022 bill setting annual enlistment targets at its first reading on 31 January 2022; in June 2024 he voted against reviving it, and since 2024 he has called for a framework under which every citizen serves.

universal-service-with-sanctions.text: That is the party's recorded position: Gantz voted for bills fining people who do not fulfil their service duty (4 February 2026) and cutting the budget of schools with low enlistment (26 November 2025). On 3 September 2026 he said that everyone at 18 must serve and "whoever doesn't serve – won't receive."

voluntary-service-for-all.text: The party's documented position is a requirement, not a voluntary option: on 3 September 2026 Gantz said everyone at 18 must serve. He also voted for a bill fining people who do not fulfil their service duty on 4 February 2026.

speed-up-planning-and-construction.text: The research found no 2026 party housing plan, and its housing section records no party position on speeding up planning and construction. Its thin, tentative indication points to direct help for buyers and to developing the north and periphery.

state-led-affordable-rental.text: The research found no 2026 party housing plan and no documented party position on state-led affordable rental. Its thin, tentative indication points to direct help for buyers and to developing the north and periphery.

direct-help-for-buyers.text: The limited evidence points to your answer, but it is thin: Gantz voted for a bill giving public-housing tenants rights to buy their homes (26 November 2025) and for reservists' priority in buying Israel Land Authority land (1 January 2025). No 2026 housing plan was found.

develop-periphery-and-transport.text: The limited evidence points to your answer, but it is thin: on 25 March 2026 Gantz voted for a bill to develop Kiryat Shmona with housing priority for reservists and disabled veterans. No 2026 housing plan was found.

military-pressure-until-threats-removed.text: This is a secondary element of the party's position: in 2026 Gantz set out a principle of no hostile presence within 10 km of the border on every front, including Lebanon. His main position pairs military pressure with US-backed agreements, which your answer excludes.

force-plus-us-backed-agreements.text: That is the party's main recorded position: as Defense Minister in October 2022 Gantz backed the US-mediated maritime border agreement with Lebanon. In May 2024 he listed advancing normalization with Saudi Arabia as one of his six conditions, and in February 2025 he called for dismantling Iran's nuclear program in coordination with the US.

prioritize-ending-multifront-war.text: The party's documented position combines military pressure with US-backed agreements: Gantz said on 14 June 2024 that Israel must act in the north through an agreement or through escalation if necessary. In 2026 he set out a principle of no hostile presence within 10 km of the border on every front.

end-military-operations-regional-peace.text: The party's documented position combines military pressure with US-backed agreements, such as normalization with Saudi Arabia, which Gantz listed as a condition in May 2024. In 2026 he set out a principle of no hostile presence within 10 km of the border on every front.

full-sovereignty.text: The party shares applying Israeli sovereignty but not its full extent: Gantz voted for applying it to the Jordan Valley (22 January 2025) and to Ma'ale Adumim (22 October 2025). The party's July 2025 alternative motion said it should be done through a national-consensus government, and Knesset records show no vote by him on the bill covering all of Judea and Samaria.

partial-sovereignty-area-c.text: That is the party's main recorded position: Gantz voted for applying Israeli sovereignty to the Jordan Valley (22 January 2025) and to Ma'ale Adumim (22 October 2025). On 18 July 2024 he also voted for a Knesset resolution opposing a Palestinian state west of the Jordan.

maintain-current-situation.text: This is a secondary element of the party's position: on 30 October 2022 Gantz proposed to "shrink the conflict", and the party's July 2025 alternative motion said sovereignty should be applied only through a national-consensus government. Its main position is applying sovereignty to key areas, which your answer excludes.

separation-two-states.text: On 30 October 2022 Gantz said of two states for two peoples, "I am against this." On 18 July 2024 he voted for a Knesset resolution opposing the establishment of a Palestinian state west of the Jordan.

two-states-pre-1967-border.text: On 30 October 2022 Gantz said of two states for two peoples, "I am against this." On 18 July 2024 he voted for a Knesset resolution opposing a Palestinian state west of the Jordan, and in January 2025 he voted to apply Israeli sovereignty to the Jordan Valley.

one-equal-state.text: On 30 October 2022 Gantz proposed to "shrink the conflict" rather than slide into "a binational state". His votes since then are for applying Israeli sovereignty to key areas: the Jordan Valley (22 January 2025) and Ma'ale Adumim (22 October 2025).

continue-judicial-changes.text: Gantz voted against the attorney general bills: splitting the role (29 October 2025) and the final reading of the attorney general law (15 July 2026). When the law changing the Judicial Selection Committee passed on 27 March 2025, he said "the politicization of the Judicial Selection Committee will be cancelled, a real reform will be advanced."

broad-agreed-constitutional-framework.text: That is the party's recorded position: in August 2026 Gantz named a constitution among the key decisions for a broad government and said the party planned to advance one. The party's 2022 list also committed to safeguarding judicial independence and the separation of powers.

repeal-changes-protect-independence.text: This is a secondary element of the party's position: when the law changing the Judicial Selection Committee passed on 27 March 2025, Gantz said its politicization "will be cancelled", and he voted against the attorney general bills in 2025 and 2026. The party's main position is a broad agreement anchored in a constitution.

keep-current-system-stability.text: When the law changing the Judicial Selection Committee passed on 27 March 2025, Gantz said "the politicization of the Judicial Selection Committee will be cancelled, a real reform will be advanced." In August 2026 he said the party planned to advance a constitution.

state-commission-under-existing-law.text: That is the party's recorded position: on 26 May 2024 Gantz, then a minister, submitted a proposed government resolution to set up a state commission of inquiry, and he voted for opposition bills for one on 17 July 2024 and 1 July 2026. The 2026 bill has the President of the Supreme Court appoint the chair and members.

commission-appointed-by-knesset-balance.text: Gantz voted against a coalition bill for a "state-national" commission on 24 December 2025, under which members would be chosen through the Knesset Speaker with coalition-opposition parity. The party instead backed bills for a state commission of inquiry (July 2024 and July 2026).

commission-chosen-by-neutral-mechanism.text: The party's documented position is a state commission of inquiry: Gantz voted for opposition bills for one on 17 July 2024 and 1 July 2026, the latter having the President of the Supreme Court appoint the chair and members.

strengthen-jewish-character.text: Gantz and the faction MKs who voted backed two private bills on public transport on Shabbat on 19 November 2025, one letting each local authority decide. On 25 February 2026 he voted against a bill to require consulting the Chief Rabbinate on holy places.

keep-status-quo.text: The research places the party at a neighboring option, with more choice and local decisions: on 19 November 2025 Gantz and the faction MKs who voted backed two bills on Shabbat public transport, one of which would let each local authority decide. That goes beyond the small local changes in your answer.

more-choice-local-decisions.text: That is the party's recorded position: Gantz and the faction MKs who voted backed two bills on public transport on Shabbat on 19 November 2025, one of which would let each local authority decide. No statement on civil marriage since 2021 was found.

separate-religion-and-state.text: The party shares Shabbat public transport but not the full separation: Gantz and the faction MKs who voted backed two public transport bills on 19 November 2025, one letting each local authority decide. The research places the party at more choice and local decisions, and found no statement on civil marriage since 2021.

points.text: Gantz has voted for a long series of private bills to support military reservists, including daycare funding for reservists' children, an income-tax credit for reserve service and a law setting up a reserves administration on 22 October 2025.
The party supports limiting how long a prime minister can serve: Gantz voted for Basic Law bills on the subject in July 2024, July 2025 and February 2026.
On 30 March 2026 Gantz and the other party MKs present voted against the final reading of the Death Penalty for Terrorists law, which passed.
